name: Hematoid Quartz
physical: Crystal healers link it to circulation of energy
Many people keep it nearby for a boost during sluggish periods
summary: Hematoid Quartz is clear quartz stained with red iron oxide, a warm, grounding stone of vitality, courage and steady drive in crystal healing tradition.
intro: Hematoid quartz, also known as fire quartz, is quartz colored red, orange or brown by inclusions of hematite or iron oxide. The color can appear as a dusting on the surface, a thick red coating, a red phantom layer inside the crystal or even as full red-stained points. Some pieces glow like embers in sunlight, while others look rusty and earthy. It is often found in Brazil and Madagascar, and the best specimens combine clear quartz with strong, saturated reds. The dramatic contrast of fire and glass is popular with collectors and with anyone who loves warm color.
history: Hematite is named from the Greek haima, meaning blood, a nod to its red streak, and red iron oxide has been used as pigment since prehistory, from cave paintings to ceremonial body paint. Hematoid quartz has been collected by mineral enthusiasts for generations, and the term hematoid simply means resembling hematite. Fire quartz is a modern trade name, and the stone has been popular since the late 20th century in crystal shops. It has little documented ancient lore, but its blood-red color connects to long traditions of using red stones for courage, life force and protection.
meaning: Hematoid quartz is a stone of vitality and courage in crystal tradition. Practitioners link its red color to the root and sacral chakras and say it brings warmth, stamina and a steady sense of drive. It is often used by people who feel sluggish, discouraged or ungrounded and want a gentle push toward action. Emotionally it is associated with confidence, resilience and calming nerves before something challenging. The quartz base is said to amplify the grounding qualities of the iron. It is also used in practices that involve movement, such as yoga and dance. Healers value it as a stone that is energizing but not harsh. Physical associations are light: vitality and circulation of energy.
howToUse: Hold a hematoid quartz point in your dominant hand while stating a goal that needs courage. Place a piece on your desk to encourage persistence during long projects. Keep a tumbled stone in your pocket on days when you feel low in energy. Wear it as a pendant near the lower belly for a warm, steady presence. Use it in a grid with carnelian and clear quartz for motivation. Set it in a spot where morning light can warm its color. Pair it with a workout or walk as a ritual, and place it away from your bed if you find it too stimulating at night.
care: Hematoid quartz is hard and handles water, so a rinse in cool water is fine. Dry it well to avoid rusty residue from surface iron. Cleanse with sunlight, moonlight, smoke or sound. Surface hematite coatings can rub off, so avoid scrubbing. Avoid sudden temperature changes and ultrasonic cleaners. Store it in a soft pouch, since the iron stains can mark light fabrics when damp, and keep it apart from softer stones that quartz may scratch.
identify: Natural hematoid quartz shows irregular red or orange iron staining inside or on the surface of clear quartz, with variations in depth and saturation. Dyed or painted stones show uniform, bright red color that pools in cracks. Iron-stained quartz with red phantoms is natural and often layered. Fakes include red glass and resin. Real quartz scratches glass and stays cool. Because surface staining can rub off onto cloth, a dye test is possible but may damage the stone. Strawberry quartz has pink inclusions and is a different variety.

faq.q: What is hematoid quartz good for?
faq.a: Hematoid quartz is traditionally used for vitality, grounding and courage. Crystal healers link it to the root and sacral chakras and say it supports steady motivation.
The red color comes from tiny inclusions or surface coatings of iron oxide minerals such as hematite. Their density determines whether the stone looks rusty, orange or deep red.

faq.q: Is hematoid quartz the same as fire quartz?
faq.a: They are used for the same stone. Fire quartz is a common trade name for hematoid quartz, especially when the red color appears as a bright coating or phantom.
